Since Brooks Hall was constructed in 1958, with approximately 100,000 net square feet of exhibition space, and Civic Auditorium was completely remodeled in 1964, the relatively slow rate of annual growth in convention delegate expenditures between 1965 and 1971 cannot be traced to a lack of first rate new convention

divided into three smaller units, the smallest of which is proposed to be approximately 50,000 net square feet in size.) The YBC exhibition hall facilities will therefore be focusing on approximately 3% of the total U.S. convention industry, or from 270 to 350 total U.S. conventions each year. If Brooks Hall's exhibition facilities are put into the equation, the total U.S. market share is reduced even further, because Brooks Hall has approximately 100,000 net square feet of exhibition space. The total U.S. demand for exhibition space above 100,000 net square feet is estimated by World Convention Dates to be 1.5% of total U.S. convention business, or 135 to 180 conventions per year. The YBC exhibition facility, if it intends to capture a share of the national market for exhibition space above 100,000 net square feet (and not compete with the 100,000 N.S.F. offered by Brooks Hall), should therefore attract and hold on some annual sustainable basis, a market share of a total national market of 135 to 180 large conventions.
